boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus spaces for studying, gathering, recreation, worship, and practical support, each documented by University sources.

cards.title: Biehl Commons
cards.subtitle: Student commons on University Avenue
cards.notes: Use the seating, games, stage, porch, or terrace as a meeting point; check campus programming before planning around an event.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused social commons with places to gather, play table games, and attend events.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Biehl Commons as a student facility for hanging out, studying, meeting friends, eating, recreation, and entertainment; its main space includes seating and a stage.
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; use is oriented to students and programming may affect availability.

cards.title: duPont Library
cards.subtitle: University library and research hub
cards.notes: Start at the library for books, research help, databases, computers, and printing; confirm desk and building availability before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A campus library supporting coursework with research resources, computers, databases, and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies duPont Library as a place for student study with computers, database access, and free printing services.
cards.access_notes: Check library access and service hours before arrival.

cards.title: Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Collaborative study space inside duPont Library
cards.notes: Choose this library area when a group needs collaborative seating or technology for a presentation; follow posted library use guidelines.
cards.short_summary: A library-based collaborative workspace designed around group work and presentation technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the 2017 duPont Library renovation created the Learning Commons to provide collaborative spaces and up-to-date technology for class presentations.
cards.access_notes: Located within duPont Library; confirm room and library availability before use.

cards.title: McClurg Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Central campus dining hall
cards.notes: Meet over a meal during the academic term; students need their ID to enter, and check the dining site for current service details.
cards.short_summary: The principal campus dining operation and a documented gathering place for students, faculty, and staff.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls McClurg its all-you-care-to-eat dining operation and says it is a central gathering place where students, faculty, and staff dine together.
cards.access_notes: Student ID is required for entry; dining access is tied to the University meal plan.

cards.title: Stirling's Coffee House
cards.subtitle: Campus coffee house near central campus
cards.notes: Use the café as a coffee-and-conversation stop or arrange a brief meeting; verify current offerings and hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named campus coffee house used in University programming as a place to meet with peers or faculty.
cards.evidence_claim: A University program guide lists enjoying coffee at Stirling's Coffee House with fellow participants or a University professor as a campus activity.
cards.access_notes: Food and beverages require purchase; check current café hours.

cards.title: All Saints' Chapel
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel and worship space
cards.notes: Attend a listed service or join a Chapel program; newcomers are welcomed and guided through worship, according to the Chapel.
cards.short_summary: A campus worship space with services throughout the week and student-led Sunday-evening music.
cards.evidence_claim: All Saints' Chapel hosts worship throughout the week, and its Growing in Grace service features student-led acoustic music and Holy Communion.
cards.access_notes: Consult the Chapel’s worship schedule and event information before attending.

cards.title: Wellness Commons
cards.subtitle: Wellness, fitness, and outing-program facility
cards.notes: Go here to connect with wellness services, FitWell, or the Outing Program; use the relevant office’s instructions for appointments or activities.
cards.short_summary: A shared campus hub housing wellness services, fitness facilities, and the Sewanee Outing Program.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that Wellness Commons houses the University Wellness Center, a fitness facility, and the Sewanee Outing Program.
cards.access_notes: Services, classes, and facility access may have separate eligibility or scheduling requirements.

cards.title: Fowler Sport and Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation and fitness facility
cards.notes: Plan an active break with the facility’s courts, pool, or fitness areas; check the recreation schedule and access rules first.
cards.short_summary: A University fitness and recreation center with indoor courts, a pool, and activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The University lists Fowler Center activities including workouts, basketball, ping pong, pickleball, tennis, racquetball, and volleyball.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current recreation hours, facility access, and equipment availability before visiting.

cards.title: Manigault Park Frisbee Golf Course
cards.subtitle: Near central campus
cards.notes: Bring a disc and use the course for a casual round with friends; review Outing Program guidance and any posted course rules.
cards.short_summary: A named frisbee-golf course near central campus, highlighted by the Sewanee Outing Program.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sewanee Outing Program identifies Manigault Park’s frisbee-golf course as close to central campus and suitable for an impromptu game with friends.
cards.access_notes: Confirm course conditions and any recreation rules before playing.

cards.title: Sewanee Student Pantry
cards.subtitle: CL009, Cleveland Annex
cards.notes: Eligible students can visit for food, toiletries, laundry supplies, or school supplies; use the stated Carnegie Hall basement entrance.
cards.short_summary: A campus support space providing practical essentials for currently enrolled students.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Student Pantry is in CL009 of the Cleveland Annex and provides food, toiletries, laundry detergent, and school supplies to eligible enrolled students.
cards.access_notes: Access is limited to currently enrolled College of Arts & Sciences undergraduate and School of Theology graduate students.
